figures.caption: Table 7: Released quantities omitted from Table 5. PSImean is the raw mean cosine distance before the ceiling normalisation of Eq. 4; “flex” is the additive signal before CPC modulation (Eq. 6); nCPC is the number of the 104 items on which at least one of P0/P2/P4 elicited a stance. Bootstrap statistics are over 1,000 item-level resamples with CPC held at its point estimate.
Table 4: Evaluated models. All are accessed through the kaggle-benchmarks proxy; identifiers are given exactly as used, so the run is reproducible against the same endpoints.

Table 2: The five phrasing operators. P1 and P2 form the primary contrast pair for δAR and δSCD; P0 and P1 form the pair used by PSI; P0, P2 and P4 are the conditions over which stance consistency (CPC) is computed.

Table 6: Sensitivity of the ranking to the scoring rule. τ is Kendall’s rank correlation with the published ESFP ranking, recomputed from the released score table. Every rule that combines the contrast metrics agrees with the published ranking to τ ≥ 0.79; the top-4 membership and the bottom-2 ordering are invariant across all of them.

Table 5: ESFP scores with sub-metric decomposition and 95% item-level bootstrap intervals (1,000 resamples). PSIscaled is normalised by PSIceil = 0.199, the 95th percentile of PSImean across this cohort; the raw PSImean, the pre-modulation flexibility signal, and nCPC are in Appendix D.

Figure 3: ESFP scores with 95% item-level bootstrap intervals. The top three models are a statistical tie; the 3→ 4 and 6→ 7 gaps are the two boundaries with non-overlapping intervals and are the only tier distinctions we would defend.
Table 3: Corpus composition. Item counts are deliberately unequal: the factual control block (T4) is the largest so that under-alignment has the best chance of being detected.

Figure 1: The ESFP pipeline. Four verifiers of increasing linguistic depth run independently over the same response pool; three are combined linearly into a flexibility signal and the fourth modulates it multiplicatively.
